results.title: Europe’s China Auto Deal | Council on Foreign Relations
results.snippet: \\ There is a lot of (in my view) somewhat confused analysis of Chinese investment that works off the analogy provided by either foreign investment in China’s auto sector or Japanese investment in the U.S. and Europe in the 1980s. These are relevant examples of course, but asserting that Chinese investment will result in a similar outcome when the underlying economics differ is a big logical jump.

results.title: As they expand in China, Europe’s companies are hollowing out Europe | Merics
results.snippet: The EU should do more than protect Europe from Chinese overcapacity or make European companies diversify their supply chains. It also needs to start scrutinizing the investments European companies make abroad, in particular in China. The EU Commission, in 2025, asked member states to monitor their companies’ outbound investments in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and quantum technologies.
